purpose: Reference lookup only. The tutor may suggest 2-3 of these topics when the participant is unsure what to discuss, filtered to their current explanation level. The participant may ask about anything within AI and Robotics, whether or not it appears here.

beginner.goal: Understand what AI is, how it differs from traditional software, and how to use modern AI tools effectively.

items: What is AI? (Artificial Intelligence vs. Machine Learning vs. Deep Learning)
How AI 'learns' from patterns in data vs. explicit programming rules
Narrow AI (Siri, ChatGPT) vs. General AI (AGI)
Types of data (structured vs. unstructured: text, images, audio, video)
Garbage in, garbage out: why data quality and diversity matter
Supervised learning: learning with labeled examples (e.g. spam filters)
Unsupervised learning: finding hidden patterns (e.g. customer segmentation)
Reinforcement learning: learning through trial and reward (e.g. AlphaGo)
How models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini generate text
Text-to-image AI (Midjourney, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion)
Core prompt engineering techniques (zero-shot, few-shot, role-based prompting)
Recommendation systems (Netflix, Spotify, TikTok)
Introduction to AI bias, fairness, and hallucination

intermediate.goal: Understand how major AI systems work under the hood, and how to build custom AI workflows.

items: Inputs, hidden layers, and outputs explained visually
Computer vision basics: how AI 'sees' objects and faces in images
NLP basics: how AI understands sentiment and context
What is the transformer architecture?
Tokens and context windows: how AI reads and remembers context
Temperature, top-p, and controlling AI output randomness
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): connecting LLMs to private data
Fine-tuning vs. prompting: when to train a custom model vs. guide an existing one
Automated workflows with tools like Zapier, Make, and Flowise
Deepfakes, copyright, and intellectual property in AI
Privacy risks: data leakage and prompt injection basics
AI alignment and human feedback (RLHF)

advanced.goal: Design multi-step AI systems, evaluate performance, and reason about AI strategy, architecture, and agents.

items: What are AI agents? (reasoning, planning, memory, tool usage)
Agentic frameworks (AutoGPT, CrewAI, LangChain architecture concepts)
Human-in-the-loop workflows for complex automation
Evaluating LLM accuracy and reliability (LLM-as-a-judge)
Measuring performance, toxicity, and hallucination
Open-source (Llama, Mistral) vs. closed-source (GPT-4, Claude) model selection
Combining text, voice, vision, and real-time interaction in one model
Real-world spatial AI, robotics, and embodied AI concepts
Build vs. buy decision frameworks for enterprise AI
AI cost optimization: token economics, caching, and latency reduction
AI regulation & compliance (EU AI Act, NIST AI Framework)
